Digital transformation has redefined Human Talent Management by incorporating analytical tools capable of converting large volumes of data into strategic information for decision-making. In this context, People Analytics and Artificial Intelligence represent key innovations for optimizing recruitment, selection, performance evaluation, talent retention, and workforce planning.This study aimed to analyze how the integration of these technologies transforms decision-making in Human Talent Management within Panamanian organizations and to propose a strategic analytical maturity model adapted to the national context. A qualitative research approach with descriptive, explanatory, and propositional scope was employed, supported by a systematic review of scientific literature, documentary analysis, and the conceptual design of the Panamanian People Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Maturity Model (MPM-PAIA). The findings indicate that organizations with greater analytical capabilities improve strategic decision-making, strengthen the efficiency of human resource processes, and enhance competitiveness. Data quality, leadership, organizational culture, analytical competencies, and ethical governance were identified as critical success factors. The study concludes that the progressive integration of People Analytics and Artificial Intelligence represents a strategic opportunity for Panamanian organizations, provided that technological adoption is accompanied by workforce development and ethical governance.

The rise of generative artificial intelligence has changed teachers' professional work, yet its use in schools depends less on technology than on leadership that builds vision, competence, support, and a culture of responsible use. Using transformational leadership theory as a lens, this study analyzes how a foundation head builds a culture of artificial intelligence utilization in a school and how the dimensions of transformational leadership appear in that process. A qualitative single case study was conducted at an Islamic elementary school in Pekanbaru, Indonesia. Data were collected on 26 August 2026 through interviews with five purposively selected teachers and the foundation head as the key informant, and were supported by observation and documentation. The data were analyzed through condensation, coding, categorization, theme development, and theoretical interpretation. The findings show that leadership operates through five interrelated mechanisms: vision and role modeling, capacity building, social learning, responsible use, and institutionalization. The foundation head demonstrated artificial intelligence use personally, organized structured training, provided facilities, encouraged peer exchange, and insisted on verifying outputs. Teachers used these tools for lesson plans, materials, assessments, and media, and practice appears to be moving from individual adoption toward institutionalized routines, although this conclusion remains tentative given the limited scope of the study. The novelty of this study is the Artificial Intelligence Transformational Leadership Pathway, a conceptual model that sequentially links the four dimensions of transformational leadership to collective norms of technology use.

This scientific article explores the transformational stages of integrating artificial intelligence and digital technologies into language teaching. It also analyzes the role of modern technologies in improving educational effectiveness, increasing students’ motivation to learn languages, and expanding opportunities for personalized learning. The benefits of using artificial intelligence-based tools, interactive platforms, and digital learning resources are examined. Furthermore, the article highlights the pedagogical opportunities and future prospects of effectively implementing these technologies in the educational process.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies has significantly transformed language teaching and learning in the twenty-first century. Traditional approaches to language education are increasingly complemented by intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning platforms, automated assessment tools, and generative AI applications. These innovations create new opportunities for personalized instruction, interactive learning, and the development of learners’ communicative competence. This article examines the transformational stages of integrating artificial intelligence and digital technologies into language teaching. It explores the transition from traditional classroom instruction to technology-enhanced learning, intelligent and adaptive education, and AI-supported personalized learning environments. Particular attention is paid to the pedagogical benefits, practical challenges, and ethical considerations associated with the implementation of these technologies. The article argues that successful digital transformation requires not only technological innovation but also pedagogically grounded implementation, teacher training, digital literacy, and responsible use of AI.

This article explores the challenges of translating Uzbek literary texts into English by comparing Shuhrat Sattorov’s English translation of Shukur Kholmirzaev’s short story “The Character of the Uzbeks” with translations produced by artificial intelligence tools. The main purpose is to identify common translation errors and examine how AI handles the linguistic, cultural, and contextual features of the original text. Special attention is given to the translation of culture-specific expressions, words with multiple meanings, sentence structures, and elements that reflect Uzbek national identity. By comparing the selected translations, the study aims to show where AI can provide clear and useful translations and where it may fail to preserve the writer’s intended meaning and cultural message.

The rapid spread of artificial intelligence-based technologies has made trust a fundamental element in the sustainable adoption of these technologies. This study aimed to adapt the Artificial Intelligence-Based Educational Technologies Trust Scale developed by Nazaretsky et al. (2022b) into Turkish in the context of prospective teachers and to examine its psychometric validity and reliability. Data were collected from 423 undergraduate students enrolled in various programs at a state university. The factor structure of the scale was analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). The fit indices of the initial 25-item model fell below acceptable thresholds. Repeated analyses resulted in a three-factor, 21-item solution. This final structure is consistent with the original dimensions, named Perceived Benefits, Perceived Barriers/Concerns, and Trust in AI-Based Educational Technologies. The fit indices for the final model were found to be acceptable (e.g., χ2/df = 1.425, RMSEA = 0.052, SRMR = 0.061). The Cronbach's alpha internal consistency coefficient for the entire scale was calculated as 0.803. The Cronbach's alpha coefficients for the subscales were 0.813, 0.684, and 0.811, respectively. Convergent and discriminant validity analyses showed that the scale is valid and reliable in its current form. These findings lay the groundwork for creating a standardized framework for monitoring and comparing trust in AI-based educational technologies among educators, policymakers, and researchers in Türkiye.
